messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap & a few sizing questions

Thanks again for the time this morning — great discussion on the integration patterns and your primary goals. High-level notes, then a few quick questions so we can size Dedicated correctly: 

Summary from call:
- FinServ Analytics is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable throughput and data isolation. Private/on-prem is on the roadmap but not required for Phase 1.
- Primary workload: real-time valuation + chat assistant embedded in internal apps. Low variance on prompt size for most calls, but some long-form generation for reports.
- Target SLA: keep 95p latency reasonable for UI interactions.

Sizing questions (can you confirm these when convenient?):
1) Desired sustained TPS (requests/sec) vs expected peak TPS (1-2x bursts)? If you prefer, give peak concurrency target instead.
2) Concurrency: how many concurrent users/requests do you expect during peak?
3) Token mix: approximate percent short prompts (<=64 tokens) vs medium (65-1024) vs long (>1024). Also average response length for the long jobs.
4) Do you have a preference for GPU family (A100-80GB vs H100)? Is cost or 95p latency the priority?
5) Any restriction on public network egress? (we can propose VPC peering / Private control plane).

Attached is a capacity worksheet we use to translate traffic into GPU footprint. If you can drop a quick sample of traffic (CSV) or answers to the above, I’ll loop in infra to propose 1-2 concrete configurations.

Next step: if you’re OK, I’ll send this to Camila + Aditya for a sizing sketch and we’ll return a short Mutual Action Plan.

Great summary — thanks, Sergio. Quick answers below (we ran a short traffic snapshot after the call and I attached it).

1) Sustained TPS: planning for ~80 sustained requests/sec initially. Peak observed in snapshot: ~220 requests/sec; operational target for spikes: up to 250 TPS for short periods (1-5 min).
2) Concurrency: estimate ~25-35 concurrent sessions at peak (many short requests per session).
3) Token mix: ~85% short prompts (user queries + single-shot responses) with avg total tokens ~40 (prompt+response). ~12% medium interactions (multi-turn summaries) avg 600 tokens. ~3% long-form reports (avg output ~1,800 tokens).
4) GPU: no hard preference yet — cost matters but we need UI 95p latency under ~400ms for short prompts. If H100 materially improves latency for your runtime, we’d consider it for the initial reservation.
5) Network: we prefer VPC peering for Dedicated (no public endpoints), but can start with dedicated-hosted and move to Private VPC if network ops needs it.

We have an internal procurement window for Q3; we want an infra sketch and a rough monthly cost ballpark to evaluate trade-offs.

Attached: initial_traffic_snapshot.csv

Thanks — Alex

Thanks for the context — good signal. Quick sizing sketch below (high-level, ballpark numbers; we should run the worksheet with the CSV for more fidelity).

Assumptions we used:
- Model: 13B- to 70B-class open model family (production performance varies); we’ll provide two-family options in the final note.
- Tokenization: short calls ~40 tokens total; medium ~600; long ~1,800.
- Target SLA: 95p latency target ~350-400ms for short prompts for UI.
- Batchability: short prompts are highly batchable; batching + KV cache reduces steady-state GPU load.

Option A — Cost-optimized (A100-80GB baseline + burst):
- Baseline: 4 x A100-80GB inference nodes (shared, reserved). This covers ~70-90 sustained TPS depending on model size and generation length with moderate batching (max_batch_size 64) and active KV caching for multi-turn.
- Burst: autoscaled pool of 8 smaller inference nodes (A100-40GB or fractionally provisioned slots) to absorb short spikes to ~250 TPS. Autoscaler policy: scale up within 90s for observed burst patterns.
- Concurrency: tune concurrency target to ~30 concurrent requests (matches their estimate).
- Expected ballpark cost: (very rough) $Xk - $Yk/month (will refine after we pick exact model & region).

Option B — Latency-optimized (H100 preference):
- Baseline: 3 x H100-class nodes (higher perf per GPU) to hit tighter 95p latency <300-350ms for short prompts and better throughput on long context work.
- Burst: keep smaller A100 nodes for cost-effective spike coverage if needed.
- Useful when customer commits to latency SLA or when model/token lengths push compute per request.

Operational notes / recommendations:
- KV/prefix caching will materially reduce GPU cycles for their multi-turn flows — it’s worthwhile to instrument sample sessions and populate the worksheet.
- Max_batch_size: start at 32-64 for short prompts; larger batches hurt tail latency but improve cost efficiency.
- Quantization: recommend Q8_0 / Q4 variants if model family supports it for cost reduction; we’ll validate quality on their eval set.
- VPC: Supported — we can propose Dedicated with VPC peering (Private control plane) as a next-phase add-on; initial deployment can be Dedicated-hosted with strict network egress rules.

Next steps I suggest we take immediately:
1) Sergio: send back worksheet filled with the traffic snapshot and mark per-route token distributions.
2) We (infra + account) finalize two concrete SKU/config cost estimates and a short MAP with timelines for PoC -> Prod.
3) If FinServ confirms model family preference, we can run a short quality + perf validation on a 48–72 hour trial cluster.

I’ll draft numbers into the worksheet and drop estimates in the HubSpot deal record.
